findings.highlight: neither accepting loss nor victory
findings.evidenceJa: 玉砕も突破もしないなんて
findings.explanation: Youko accuses Kazusa of neither charging to a glorious defeat nor breaking through to victory. The translation turns active, risky attempts into passively accepting outcomes and weakens the criticism that Kazusa refuses to commit either way.
findings.japanese:
「じゃあ介入ついでにもう一言。
…玉砕も突破もしないなんて、
そんなふうに、人生逃げちゃっていいの？」
findings.todokanai: "In that case, I might as well intervene just a bit further… Are you sure you should be running away from your life like that, neither accepting loss nor victory?"

findings.highlight: I consider raising a child all by myself a victory.
findings.evidenceJa: 子供一人くらい産んで育てるのは、楽勝だって思ってた
findings.explanation: Youko says she thought giving birth to and raising one child would be easy. 楽勝 means an easy win, not that she regards the eventual act as a victory; the mistranslation removes her youthful overconfidence.
findings.japanese:
「べっつに～。
子供一人くらい産んで育てるのは、
楽勝だって思ってたからね」
findings.todokanai: "Not really. After all, I consider raising a child all by myself a victory."

findings.highlight: I'd at least consider if my actions are ruining someone's life… At least if doing so doesn't ruin my own life.
findings.evidenceJa: 相手の人生を壊さないって配慮は評価するけどね。…それで自分が壊れずに済むなら
findings.explanation: Youko gives Kazusa credit for taking care not to destroy Haruki's life—but only if that restraint lets Kazusa survive intact. The translation makes Youko consider her own acts and her own life, losing the warning directed at her daughter.
findings.japanese:
「相手の人生を壊さないって配慮は評価するけどね。
…それで自分が壊れずに済むなら」
findings.todokanai: "I'd at least consider if my actions are ruining someone's life… At least if doing so doesn't ruin my own life."

findings.highlight: I saw Takeya and his old friend sitting at a table.
findings.evidenceJa: テーブル席の方に陣取ってた、腐れ縁の仲間たち
findings.explanation: Haruki sees the whole group of long-entangled friends occupying a table, including Io, Tomo, Takeya, and Setsuna. The translation reduces the plural party to Takeya and a single old friend.
findings.japanese:
どこかで聞いた男っぽい女声に振り向くと、
テーブル席の方に陣取ってた、腐れ縁の仲間たち。
findings.todokanai: Instead, I heard the chatter of a woman with a rather masculine voice, and when I turned to it, I saw Takeya and his old friend sitting at a table.

findings.highlight: everything just continued to develop even more quickly than I expected
findings.evidenceJa: 事実は真実に、約束は契約へと、予想を越えて成長していった
findings.explanation: As the rumor grows, a fact becomes 'truth' and a promise becomes a binding contract, exceeding Haruki's prediction in substance. The English repeats the previous line's speed joke and loses the escalating distortion of engagement status.
findings.japanese:
そして事実は真実に、
約束は契約へと、
予想を越えて成長していった。
findings.todokanai: The facts became truth, a promise became a binding contract, and everything just continued to develop even more quickly than I expected.

findings.highlight: they're ignoring her reaction despite the fact that it's happening right before their very eyes
findings.evidenceJa: そんな重要なやり取りがあったなんて全然気づかず
findings.explanation: The friends completely fail to notice the decisive emotional exchange occurring before them. The translation says they notice but ignore Setsuna's reaction, reversing their information state.
findings.japanese:
けれど皆、自分たちの目の前で
そんな重要なやり取りがあったなんて全然気づかず、
雪菜をからかって盛り上がってた。
findings.todokanai: Even so, they're ignoring her reaction despite the fact that it's happening right before their very eyes, completely focused on teasing Setsuna.

findings.highlight: How I'm the slightest bit worried.
findings.evidenceJa: 露ほども悩んでなんかいないって
findings.explanation: The 'good lie' is that Haruki is not worried in the slightest. The translation drops the negation and makes him lie that he is a little worried, the opposite of Kazusa's prescribed performance.
findings.japanese:
曇り一つなく喜んでいるって。
露ほども悩んでなんかいないって。
findings.todokanai: To lie about how I'm undoubtedly happy. How I'm the slightest bit worried.

findings.highlight: things started to get awkward between you two after that
findings.evidenceJa: 帰ってきてからずっとテンション高かった気がする
findings.explanation: Io says Setsuna seemed continuously high-spirited after returning from her Osaka trip. The translation invents awkwardness between the couple, feeding the next lines a false premise.
findings.japanese:
「そういえば先月、
初めて泊まりの出張行ってきたんだってね。
帰ってきてからずっとテンション高かった気がする」
findings.todokanai: "Speaking of work, she went on her first business trip last month, right? I feel that things started to get awkward between you two after that."

findings.highlight: the proposal happened because of something dramatic that has something to do with that awkwardness
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜のテンションを左右する劇的なきっかけがあったことは、今日この場で証明された
findings.explanation: Tomo says today's party proves a dramatic trigger occurred that affected Setsuna's mood. The translation asserts that the proposal was caused by an event related to invented awkwardness, changing both the proven effect and causal chain.
findings.japanese:
「つい最近、雪菜のテンションを左右する
劇的なきっかけがあったことは、
今日この場で証明された訳なんですけど」
findings.todokanai: "I think we have already established that the proposal happened because of something dramatic that has something to do with that awkwardness."

findings.highlight: I started wondering if the job didn't go as planned
findings.evidenceJa: だからてっきり仕事で上手く行ったのかと
findings.explanation: Because Setsuna changed around the trip, Io had assumed something went well at work. The translation inserts 'didn't,' reversing the explanation for her elevated mood.
findings.japanese:
「でも、明らかに出張の前後で態度が違ったんだよ。
だからてっきり仕事で上手く行ったのかと…」
findings.todokanai: "But it started happening right around the time of her business trip. So I started wondering if the job didn't go as planned…"

findings.highlight: the number I sent her will have to change
findings.evidenceJa: 今日あいつに送るメッセージに含まれる数字は、『遅くなる』じゃなくて『帰らない』になってしまうかも
findings.explanation: Haruki fears that the message he sends Kazusa tonight may need the 'not coming home' code instead of 'late.' The English treats the number as already sent but somehow still changeable, corrupting the sequence of coded updates.
findings.japanese:
このままじゃ、
今日あいつに送るメッセージに含まれる数字は、
『遅くなる』じゃなくて『帰らない』になってしまうかも。
findings.todokanai: If this goes on any longer, then the number I sent her will have to change from 1 "I'll be late" to 2 "I can't come home today."

findings.highlight: run into her exiting my apartment
findings.evidenceJa: もし、外に出た瞬間に鉢合わせしてしまったら
findings.explanation: Haruki fears the group could meet disguised Kazusa the moment she steps outside her neighboring room after receiving his warning. The translation has her exit Haruki's apartment, which would be far more direct evidence of the affair.
findings.japanese:
それに、たとえ連絡が取れたとしても、
もし、外に出た瞬間に鉢合わせしてしまったら…
findings.todokanai: And even if I manage to get in contact with her, if we were to run into her exiting my apartment…

findings.highlight: It would seem that the engagement between Setsuna and me gave those two, who had spent more time with each other than with either of us, a lot of courage about facing one another.
findings.evidenceJa: あいつに、大きな勇気を与えたらしかった
findings.explanation: Haruki and Setsuna's apparent result gives Takeya specifically the courage to act about Io. The translation says it gives both Takeya and Io courage, inventing reciprocity not established in the scene.
findings.japanese:
俺と雪菜の出した“結果”は、
俺たち以上の腐れ縁を持て余すあいつに、
大きな勇気を与えたらしかった。
findings.todokanai: It would seem that the engagement between Setsuna and me gave those two, who had spent more time with each other than with either of us, a lot of courage about facing one another.

findings.highlight: For a long time, it looked like Kazusa felt sympathy for him.
findings.evidenceJa: 長い時間、強い想いを持ち続けることに、かずさはシンパシーを感じているみたいだった
findings.explanation: Kazusa empathizes with the act of sustaining powerful feelings for a long time. The translation instead says she has sympathized with Takeya for a long time, changing both object and duration.
findings.japanese:
長い時間、強い想いを持ち続けることに、
かずさはシンパシーを感じているみたいだった。
findings.todokanai: For a long time, it looked like Kazusa felt sympathy for him.

findings.highlight: before long, she found herself sympathizing with Setsuna too, and her feelings became complicated
findings.evidenceJa: 突き詰めれば雪菜の想いにも共感してしまうという、あまりにも矛盾した感情
findings.explanation: Taken to its conclusion, Kazusa's empathy for long devotion forces her to empathize with Setsuna's love as well—an acutely self-contradictory feeling. 'Before long' makes it a temporal development and generic complication.
findings.japanese:
けどそれは、
突き詰めれば雪菜の想いにも共感してしまうという、
あまりにも矛盾した感情で…
findings.todokanai: But before long, she found herself sympathizing with Setsuna too, and her feelings became complicated…

findings.highlight: guide the conversation to one about my best friend, to ease her mind
findings.evidenceJa: かずさの言葉を軽く流し、移り気で一本気という、矛盾した友達の話を続けようと
findings.explanation: Haruki brushes Kazusa's self-condemnation aside and tries to continue discussing his contradictory friend, fickle yet single-minded. The translation omits that defining contradiction and invents an explicit aim to ease her mind.
findings.japanese:
だから、俺はかずさの言葉を軽く流し、
移り気で一本気という、矛盾した友達の話を続けようと…
findings.todokanai: So I decided to guide the conversation to one about my best friend, to ease her mind.

findings.highlight: That sounds rough…
findings.evidenceJa: それは…耳が痛いな
findings.explanation: Kazusa says Haruki's criticism hits painfully close to home because it also describes them. The translation treats it as merely a rough situation and loses the line's rebound onto their affair.
findings.japanese: 「それは…耳が痛いな」
findings.todokanai: "That sounds rough…"

findings.highlight: I decided to forget about all the unpleasant things in my life
findings.evidenceJa: 嫌なことはなるべく忘れようって、本能的に記憶から消されてるのかも
findings.explanation: Kazusa speculates that unpleasant things may be instinctively erased from her memory as self-protection. The translation makes this a conscious decision, contradicting 本能的 and her uncertainty.
findings.japanese:
「…嫌なことはなるべく忘れようって、
本能的に記憶から消されてるのかもな」
findings.todokanai: "…I decided to forget about all the unpleasant things in my life, so I may have forgotten about it instinctively."

findings.highlight: who Kazusa had a rather poor impression of
findings.evidenceJa: かずさにとっては印象の薄い『俺の親友』
findings.explanation: Takeya simply left little impression on Kazusa; she barely remembers him. 'Poor impression' says she actively viewed him negatively.
findings.japanese:
それからも俺たちは、
かずさにとっては印象の薄い『俺の親友』話で、
ゆっくりと流れる穏やかな時間を過ごす。
findings.todokanai: After that, time slowly and uneventfully passed between us as we continued to talk about my best friend, who Kazusa had a rather poor impression of.

findings.highlight: the women who were actually present thereーincluding Setsunaーweren't among us
findings.evidenceJa: その場に女性陣は…雪菜は、いなかった
findings.explanation: Within Haruki's sustained lie, he and Takeya drank alone and the women—Setsuna especially—were not there. The English injects that they were 'actually present,' exposing the truth inside the sentence that is supposed to formulate the lie.
findings.japanese:
俺と武也は最初から最後まで男二人で飲んでいて、
その場に女性陣は…雪菜は、いなかった。
findings.todokanai: It was only Takeya and me drinking from beginning to end, while the women who were actually present thereーincluding Setsunaーweren't among us.

findings.highlight: she timidly grabs my hands, entwines her fingers with mine and squeezes them tightly
findings.evidenceJa: おそるおそる触れてくるかずさの手を、指もしっかり絡めて、ぎゅっと握り締める
findings.explanation: Kazusa only reaches out timidly; Haruki catches her hand, firmly intertwines their fingers, and squeezes. The translation assigns all decisive reassurance to Kazusa.
findings.japanese:
そして、おそるおそる触れてくるかずさの手を、
指もしっかり絡めて、ぎゅっと握り締める。
findings.todokanai: And in response, she timidly grabs my hands, entwines her fingers with mine and squeezes them tightly.

findings.highlight: strokes my cheeks over and over again
findings.evidenceJa: 何度も頬ずりを繰り返す
findings.explanation: Kazusa repeatedly nuzzles or rubs her cheek against Haruki while cradling his head. The translation changes mutual face contact into her hand stroking his cheeks.
findings.japanese:
俺の背中を胸で受け止めて、
頭を抱え込み、何度も頬ずりを繰り返す。
findings.todokanai: She supports my back with her chest, holds her arms around my head, and strokes my cheeks over and over again.

findings.highlight: She hits me with her warm emotions.
findings.evidenceJa: 熱い気持ちを、吹きかける
findings.explanation: Following her warm breath against his neck, Kazusa 'breathes' her hot feelings onto him by saying she loves him. The translation replaces the linked physical-verbal image with an aggressive, abstract hit.
findings.japanese: 熱い気持ちを、吹きかける。
findings.todokanai: She hits me with her warm emotions.

findings.highlight: As we went on living our lives without each other, a wall grew between us that could no longer be crossed with just our feelings alone.
findings.evidenceJa: 距離も立場も進むべき未来も…
findings.explanation: The English assigned to line 374 translates the full thought from line 375, while line 375 receives only line 374's fragment about distance, standing, and future. Continuous meaning survives, but the line mapping and rhetorical order are reversed.
findings.japanese: 距離も立場も進むべき未来も…
findings.todokanai: As we went on living our lives without each other, a wall grew between us that could no longer be crossed with just our feelings alone.

findings.highlight: decided to get close to the two girls you thought of as number one and number two
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の中のナンバー１とナンバー２に、ただ、無節操に甘えてただけなのか
findings.explanation: Kazusa asks whether Haruki indiscriminately imposed on and depended upon the two top-ranked girls. The translation reduces that ethically charged reliance to simply getting close to them.
findings.japanese:
「自分の中のナンバー１とナンバー２に、
ただ、無節操に甘えてただけなのか…？」
findings.todokanai: "So you just decided to get close to the two girls you thought of as number one and number two…?"

findings.highlight: calculating, vindictive man
findings.evidenceJa: 計算高くて執念深い奴
findings.explanation: Kazusa calls Haruki calculating and obsessively persistent or tenacious in pursuing her. 執念深い does not make him vindictive; revenge is not her accusation.
findings.japanese:
「なんて…なんて計算高くて執念深い奴なんだ。
そんな、そんな…」
findings.todokanai: "…You're such a calculating, vindictive man… to think… to think…"

findings.highlight: All she could do was…
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬かずさっていう、とんでもない馬鹿なら…
findings.explanation: The Japanese trails on the conditional thought 'if it is that extraordinary idiot Touma Kazusa…' before her speech. The English appends a new unfinished claim, 'All she could do was,' with no source predicate or continuation.
findings.japanese:
俺を五年間ずっと忘れなかった、
冬馬かずさっていう、とんでもない馬鹿なら…
findings.todokanai: Because Touma Kazusa is a preposterous idiot who couldn't forget about me for five whole years. All she could do was…

findings.highlight: the woman you caught is really bad at giving up
findings.evidenceJa: 諦めの悪い女に引っかかっちゃってなぁ
findings.explanation: Kazusa jokes that Haruki has had the bad luck to get caught by or tangled up with a woman who will not give up. The translation makes her the woman he caught, reversing agency in the trap image.
findings.japanese:
「残念だったな、春希…
諦めの悪い女に引っかかっちゃってなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "Too bad, Haruki… the woman you caught is really bad at giving up."

findings.highlight: a peaceful look on her face
findings.evidenceJa: ものすごく満たされた顔で眠ってた
findings.explanation: Kazusa sleeps looking profoundly fulfilled or satisfied after their night of mutual confession. 'Peaceful' keeps calmness but loses the sense that her longing has been filled.
findings.japanese:
かずさは、俺が揺り起こすまで、
ものすごく満たされた顔で眠ってた。
findings.todokanai: Until I shook her awake, Kazusa slept with such a peaceful look on her face.
